# Accelerating Cavities

Two copper cavities in the ring restore the energy each electron radiates on every
turn and provide the longitudinal focusing that keeps bunches short. They are
driven by klystron amplifiers through a circulator and waveguide run from the
gallery.

Each cavity carries a mechanical plunger whose insertion depth shifts the resonant
frequency. The cavity tuner loop moves that plunger to hold the phase between the
forward wave and the cavity field at its setpoint as the copper heats up under
beam loading.

Cavity temperature is held by an independent water skid; a swing of one degree is
enough to walk the resonance far enough that the plunger reaches an end stop.

Interlocks watch the reflected power, the vacuum in the cavity body, and the arc
detectors in the waveguide, and any of them will inhibit the drive within
microseconds. See [Low-Level RF Control](/rf/low_level_rf_control.md) for the
regulation that sits upstream of the amplifier.
